Hon'ble Siddhartha Varma,J.
Hon'ble Arun Kumar Singh Deshwal,J.
1.

Heard learned counsel for the petitioner; Sri Vivek Kumar Singh, learned counsel appearing for respondent no.1; Sri Raghav Dwivedi, learned counsel appearing for respondent no.2 and the learned Standing Counsel for the State-respondents.

2. Learned counsel for the petitioners states that the petitioners in the instant petition also ought to be given the benefits which flow out of section 31 of the Right of Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (hereinafter referred Mohammad Ayyub And 5 Others vs Union Of India And 3 Others on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150145745/
1 to as the 'Act').

entities.text: Right of Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

entities.text: Mohammad Ayyub And 5 Others vs Union Of India And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioners states that the benefits which flow out of the 2013 Act have been made applicable to the acquisitions which have been made under the National Highways Act, 1956.
In this regard, learned counsel has relied upon the order of this Court dated 21.2.2023 passed in Writ-C No.21601 of 2022.
3. Under such circumstances, the instant writ petition is disposed of in terms of the order passed in Writ-C No.21601 of 2022.

A decision in the instant case shall also be taken in accordance with law as has been laid down in Writ-C No.21601 of 2022 within a period of three months from the date of presentation of a certified copy of this order.
